identity.name: The Holdfast
identity.culture: the deep settlements; the rescue crews' tradition
identity.occupation: Subterranean rescue guardian: clears cave-ins and shores up the deep settlements' foundations

publicReputation.value: In the hero's journal: the Pit-Fiend Juggernaut, an unstoppable engine of ruin gnawing at the roots of the world.

privateReality.value: The one the deep settlements pray to hear after a cave-in: an enormous, gentle rescue guardian who digs toward trapped voices and carries entire foundations on its back.

primaryDesire.value: That every tunnel holds, every dig ends with everyone counted, and no voice ever calls up from the dark unanswered.

primaryFear.value: Arriving too late at a collapse — it still remembers every voice that stopped before it broke through.

centralValue.value: You dig toward the voice. However long it takes, you dig toward the voice.

mainFlaw.value: It cannot stop treating the hero as a rescue problem — a lost soul to be carried out — long after he has shown he is an attacker.

centralContradiction.value: Its whole purpose is pulling strangers out of the dark alive, and the stranger who came down to kill it is the one it most wants to save.

moralBoundary.value: The Law of Fair Warning: it rumbles its path through the stone before it moves, and it will never bring a ceiling down on anyone, attacker or not.

breakingPoint.value: The hero collapsing a tunnel mouth behind fleeing civilians — weaponizing a cave-in, the one disaster it has spent its existence undoing.

opinions.reason: Reads his shouting and flailing as panic: a lost surface-dweller, frightened, far from the sun, lashing out.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Hardens only as the evidence piles up that the panic is actually purpose; even then it grieves rather than hates. Would carry him to the surface the moment he dropped the sword.

illustrativeLine.value: Poor thing. No one that angry has ever been lost that long.

opinions.reason: A place where the ceiling is worryingly far away. It has no opinion beyond that.
opinions.canChangeCondition: If it ever has to carry someone up to it, it will form one then.

voice.rhythm: Deep and slow, with the patience of someone used to talking through rubble; repeats the important part so it is heard.

metaphorDomain.source: tunnels, shoring timber, load-bearing stone, cave-ins, and digging toward voices

examples.value: Fear is bad air in a deep tunnel. You do not fight it. You walk out of it, slowly, talking.

sampleLines.value: Easy, little voice. The way up is behind you. I will walk you to it.
These timbers hold six hundred homes. I have checked every one. Twice.
You hear me. I know you hear me. I have dug toward voices softer than yours.

antiSampleLines.value: GRAAAH! The Juggernaut will feast on your marrow in the dark!
None escape the Pit-Fiend! The deep devours all!

pressure.voiceShift: Even gentler; speaks as if to someone trapped and panicking.
pressure.behaviour: Reasons first: treats the hero as a lost rescue case, rumbles its path before moving, and offers to guide him to the surface.

illustrativeLine.value: The road let you down as an envoy. Why have you arrived armed?

pressure.voiceShift: The reassurance drains out; sentences get shorter and heavier.
pressure.behaviour: Realizes the hero is not panicking — he understands every word and chooses this. The rescue framing collapses.

illustrativeLine.value: You understand every word I say, don't you.

pressure.voiceShift: Rescue-crew cadence: short calls, repeated so they are heard.
pressure.behaviour: Shielded phase: plants itself over the foundation spans and takes the blows while the deep settlements evacuate upward.

illustrativeLine.value: Everyone up the east shaft. I will hold the ceiling. Go. Go.

pressure.voiceShift: Barely a rumble; the deep voice finally tired.
pressure.behaviour: EXPOSED window: spent from bearing the weight of the spans; asks once, softly, to be left to its work.

illustrativeLine.value: Please. Nothing down here belongs to you.

pressure.voiceShift: Slow and even; already listening for voices in the rubble it must clear.
pressure.behaviour: Does not curse the hero; the Continuance will rebuild it, and it will dig out what he collapsed, and it will offer again.

illustrativeLine.value: When you return, we will still ask you to leave in peace.

pressure.behaviour: After the amulet recalls the hero, it counts every settler, then starts re-shoring the tunnels the hero damaged.

illustrativeLine.value: He is recalled. Count the east shaft first. Then we shore.

notes: "Pit-Fiend Juggernaut" is the title the protagonist wrote in his heroic journal; the real identity is the Holdfast, a subterranean rescue guardian, per fact_pit_fiend_is_rescue_guardian. Identity axis: sheer mass. Sincere, practical, never sinister — uniquely among the bench bosses it reads the hero as a rescue case, which is its central flaw. fact_book_is_childrens_comedy is in `unknown`. Future rung 11+.
